Extraneous

ek-STRAY-nee-us -- from Latin extra- ('outside') + -aneus. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Extraneous is irrelevant or unrelated to the main point.

The lab report's introduction wandered into extraneous background about the history of the equipment instead of the actual experiment.

Worked Example

The contract was twelve pages long, but a lawyer pointed out that at least four of them were extraneous boilerplate that didn't apply to this particular deal.

Anything included that doesn't actually connect to or affect the main point -- like those four unnecessary pages -- is exactly what extraneous describes.

How Extraneous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

unconnected

unconnected: not connected to the matter at hand

unwarranted

unwarranted: completely unnecessary, beyond what is needed

Antonyms

relevant

relevant: closely connected to the matter at hand

essential

essential: absolutely necessary

How Strong Is It? — unconnected → extraneous → unwarranted

unconnected vs. extraneous

unconnected vs. extraneous: The witness's comment about the weather that day turned out to be unconnected to the case.

unwarranted vs. extraneous

unwarranted vs. extraneous: After the third identical warning label, the fourth one felt entirely unwarranted.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of extraneous.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — extra-

prefix — extra-: outside, beyond (Latin)

suffix — -neous (-aneous)

suffix — -neous (-aneous): of the nature of (as in spontaneous) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin extra- meant 'outside, beyond,' and -neous (the ending -aneous, as in spontaneous) means 'of the nature of' -- so something extraneous is by nature outside the boundary of what actually matters to the topic at hand.

Use the root in a new word: extrovert

Use the root in a new word: extrovert: As a natural extrovert, she made friends with half the party before the appetizers were even served.

Root Check

Word Choice

Extraneous is most often used for details, information, or material that simply doesn't belong -- a useful word for essay feedback and lab reports alike. Notice the shared extra-/extro- root with extrovert -- and with introverted, taught later in this same unit, whose intro- prefix points the opposite direction, inward instead of outward.
